title: A three-weight obstruction for two copies of 3P_2 join O_2: a counterexample to Lau-Shiu Conjecture 4.1 on local antimagic chromatic numbers (arXiv:2410.17674; Utilitas Math. 124 (2025))
exact_endpoint: not_conjecture41 : ¬ Conjecture41, where Conjecture41 := ∀ r s m : ℕ, 1 ≤ r → 1 ≤ s → 2 ≤ m → Antimagic.chiLA (LauShiu.graph r s m) = 3; LauShiu.graph r s m is the SimpleGraph 2r((2s+1)P_2 join O_m) and chiLA is the least colour count of local antimagic labellings (edge bijections onto 1..|E| with distinct weights on adjacent vertices), the definitions reused byte-identically from the accepted 354228 packet
scope: Lau-Shiu Conjecture 4.1: chi_la(2r((2s+1)P_2 join O_m)) = 3 for r, s >= 1 and m >= 2. False at r = s = 1, m = 2: the 16-vertex graph 2(3P_2 join O_2) has no local antimagic labelling with at most three weights (and chi_la = 4 by an explicit labelling, supporting).
formalization_lanes: expanded-corpus-r159 (instantiated obstruction); joinla-formal-r2 (literal general family, literal chi_la and bridges; 7 modules)

substantive_reason: It refutes a 2025 published universal conjecture on local antimagic chromatic numbers of joins, which the authors posed after proving every other parity case. The proof is a complete counting obstruction: the equal-null-weight case has an older parity analogue (Chan-Lau-Shiu, chi_la(C_3 + C_3) = 4), and the new content closes the exchanged-null-role case through the six common-weight endpoints and twelve distinct join labels. Significance is modest: a short argument at the smallest admissible instance.
